In its fiscal 2021 10-K, NRG says acquisitions and dispositions of businesses, assets, or retail customer books involve a number of risks [1].

**Acquisition risks:** failing to identify material problems during due diligence, overpaying for assets or customers, being unable to retain customers, and being unable to arrange needed financing. Integration also requires substantial human, financial and other resources, and the acquisitions may not be successfully integrated [1].

**Disposition risks:** employment matters, and risks involving counterparties, regulators and other stakeholders in the disposed business. Others are separating the disposed assets from NRG's business, managing NRG's ongoing business, risks unknown to NRG at the time, and other financial, legal and operational risks. NRG may also face material trailing liabilities from disposed businesses [1].

**Possible consequences:** these risks may lead to costly disputes or litigation. There is no assurance that acquisitions will perform as expected or that their returns will support the debt incurred or the capital expenditures needed. There is also no assurance that NRG will realize the anticipated benefits of dispositions. Failing to realize the anticipated returns or benefits could adversely affect NRG's results of operations, cash flows and financial condition [1].
